text.en: Lizard of the Meuse (Latin Mosa), the river at Maastricht

timeRange.note: Harrell and Martin (2015) give upper Campanian to uppermost Maastrichtian, just below the K/Pg boundary. ICS has no upper-Campanian boundary, so the start uses the base of the Campanian (83.6 Ma); the true first appearance is younger.

lengthM.note: Estimate of about 17 m for one exceptionally large individual from Penza, Russia, based on a partial skull; most individuals were smaller.

discovery.note: Mantell named the species in 1829; PBDB dates the genus name Mosasaurus to 1822.

text.en: Mosasaurus was a huge sea-going reptile, not a dinosaur, that hunted in the seas of the Late Cretaceous. It had a powerfully built lower jaw. Its fossils come from Europe, Africa, Asia and North America. One giant from Penza in Russia, known from a partial skull, is estimated at about 17 metres long, one of the largest mosasaurs ever found. Mosasaurus survived until just before the mass extinction 66 million years ago.

uncertain.note: The Campanian start depends on North American 'Mosasaurus maximus' records, which Harrell and Martin (2015) treat as M. hoffmannii; Polish Upper Campanian material is an uncertain identification.
